unmapped_findings: For the 17Al alloy, at the low aging temperature of 525 °C the hardness increases only gradually and the alloy fails to reach its peak hardness (b0038); the 525 °C series remains the lowest of all aging temperatures (~570-620 HV at 10 h) (figure_002).

The increase in Al content significantly slows the aging hardening response: at aging temperatures from 525 °C to 575 °C the aging hardening response of the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys significantly slowed down with increasing Al content (b0038).

For the 17Al and 19Al alloys aged at 525 °C, the precipitation of β-Mn was very slow compared to the 15Al alloy, and only a small amount of β-Mn was observed even after 10 h of aging (b0053); this behavior is consistent with the 17Al 525 °C / 10 h EBSD result where only 20.5 % β-Mn formed along α grain boundaries and within α grains, with some small α-Mn particles in the α matrix (b0041).
